title: Icecrown
body: Icecrown is the frozen crown of Northrend and the Lich King's own domain. Over it rises Icecrown Citadel, the seat of the master of the Scourge, who was once Arthas Menethil, prince of Lordaeron. The land around the citadel is his fortress. Three great gates, Mord'rethar, Aldur'thar and Corp'rethar, bar the road to its walls, the Cult of the Damned serves at his gates and in his cathedral, and the vrykul of Jotunheim fight one another for the honor of joining his chosen at Ymirheim. Every power that would see him ended has come. The Argent Crusade has broken through the southeastern mountains, the Knights of the Ebon Blade strike from Death's Rise and from smaller camps across the glacier, and the gunships Skybreaker and Orgrim's Hammer hang above the battlefield, where the Alliance and the Horde fight the Scourge and each other. In the far west, the last of the Scarlet Onslaught holds a harbor of its own.

parts.body: In the northeast of Icecrown, the Argent Crusade has raised the grounds of a great tournament beside a new coliseum. Heroes of the Alliance and the Horde, and knights of the Ebon Blade, come to test their skill against one another, so that the strongest will be ready when the time comes to face their common enemy.

title: The Argent Vanguard
body: The Argent Vanguard is the Argent Crusade's walled camp in the southeastern reaches of Icecrown, raised where the Crusade forced its way into the Lich King's land after the Alliance and the Horde had failed. Highlord Tirion Fordring commands here, and the camp is under siege. Nerubians of the Forgotten Depths swarm through the Valley of Echoes to the west, where captured crusaders lie webbed on the field as living shields. In the Vanguard Infirmary at the camp's heart Father Gustav fights a venom no one can cure, and Penumbrius of the bronze dragonflight keeps the proto-drakes that fly for the Crusade.

parts.body: The chill of death stirred in the west, and the Lich King answered the Crusade's breach with an assault on the Vanguard itself. Siegemaster Fezzik readied the camp's defenses at the front gate: atop each of its four towers stood a retractable cannon, blessed by Father Gustav, and Argent champions took the field in the valley below.

title: Scourgeholme and the Breach
body: Beyond the Valley of Echoes, the Breach is the gap the Argent Crusade blew through the mountain wall, and past it lies Scourgeholme, the first Scourge encampment within Icecrown. It is a Nerubian stronghold of the Forgotten Depths, raised in tiers: Salranax the Flesh Render lords over the temple on the first, High Priest Yath'amon preaches at the spirit tower on the second, and Underking Talonox holds court in the Pit of Fiends up the high road. The Crusade charged in when the wall came down and was thrown back, leaving many soldiers behind, and the Lich King himself has been seen among its defenders.

parts.body: When the Lich King's assault on the Vanguard failed, Scourgeholme turned to slash and burn: the crusaders it held captive were to be executed and raised in his service, and reanimated crusaders now walk its tiers where the prisoners once lay.

title: Crusaders' Pinnacle
body: Crusaders' Pinnacle is a high crag above the Breach, named by the Scourge in mockery of the Argent crusaders whose skulls they piled upon it. The land falls away from it toward Scourgeholme and the heart of Icecrown, and whoever holds its height holds a foothold inside the very walls of the Lich King's domain. The Crusade has not forgotten what was done to its dead there.

parts.body: The Crusade took the pinnacle back. Crusader Lord Dalfors and his priests burned what the Scourge had made of their dead, and a blessed banner of the Crusade, planted atop the skulls, sanctified the ground while the Scourge threw wave after wave against it. The Lich King's voice rang over the field, driving his creations on, and still the pinnacle held.

title: Onslaught Harbor and Death's Rise
body: Off Icecrown's western coast the Scarlet Onslaught holds an island harbor, manned by battle-hardened veterans of New Hearthglen in the Dragonblight. Guards, paladins and raven bishops walk its docks, the Crimson Cathedral has a single, heavily guarded entrance, and gryphon riders patrol the sky, while two ships ride at anchor under Captains Welsington and Hartford. On the cliff above stands Death's Rise, where the Knights of the Ebon Blade under Lord-Commander Arete mean to end the Onslaught once and for all, though the Argent Crusade turns a blind eye to it. His knights raise the Scarlet dead into the very thing they hated, ride bone gryphons made from captured Onslaught mounts, and search the enemy's trunks for each day's plans.

title: The Shadow Vault
body: The Shadow Vault is a Scourge stronghold cut into the mountains of northern Icecrown, where the death knight General Lightsbane oversees the forging of new weapons. Above its spires floats the Ocular, an eye through which the Lich King watches over the vault. Cultists, geists and ravenous ghouls crowd its grounds and death knight masters keep its yards, while on its ledges and middle tier wait three of the Lich King's servants: the abomination Vile, the banshee Lady Nightswood and a one-eyed geist called the Leaper.

parts.body: The Shadow Vault has fallen to the Knights of the Ebon Blade. The Ocular was destroyed to blind the Lich King. Baron Sliver, who had only feigned loyalty, broke Vile, Nightswood and the Leaper from his will with a sovereign rod, and General Lightsbane fell beside his own forge. Duke Lankral commands the vault now, and its knights fight tooth and nail to hold it against the Scourge.

title: Jotunheim
body: Jotunheim is a vrykul city over the mountains west of the Shadow Vault, where its people were first reawakened, a place second only to Ymirheim in their hearts. Its warriors are forever challenging one another to ascend: the victors go to Ymirheim to join the Lich King's elite, and the losers are reduced to vargul. They spar on the Savage Ledge below the hall of Thane Ufrang the Mighty, fight with honor on Battlescar Spire and let ancient heroes slumber in the Halls of the Ancestors, while oracles in Kul'galar Keep scry through the Eye of the Lich King. Overthane Balargarde, master of Jotunheim, rules from his fortress on its southwestern edge.

title: Njorndar Village and the Underhalls
body: Njorndar Village lies in the southwest of greater Jotunheim, home to spear-sisters, water magi and the proto-drakes the vrykul ride to war. Beside it a water lock teems with elementals the magi have yet to tame, and in a cave on the village's south side the bone witch throws her bones. To the northeast the Underhalls burrow into the mountain. There, by the Lich King's leave, a mad scientist known as Dr. Terrible experiments on vargul, and a massive flesh giant stands still at the end of the Hall of Horrors. Below lies the Circle of Suffering, where Thane Illskar keeps his champions, and a vargul named Bethod Feigr broods alone on his shame.

parts.body: Bethod Feigr was Thane Ufrang's champion until his fight for ascendance in Valhalas, when Thane Illskar sabotaged him with dark magic and he lost, to be reduced to a vargul. His prayers to the Lady of the Sword were answered: a challenger threw down his sword before Illskar in the Circle of Suffering, and the thane died for his treachery.

title: Valhalas
body: Valhalas is the vrykul's sacred battle pit, north of Njorndar Village, where warriors fight for their ascendance and the corpses of the fallen stand as a testament to the strength of their ways. Those who prove unworthy are reduced to vargul. The val'kyr Geirrvif presides over its challenges, and from the southern lip the vrykul death knight Gjonner the Merciless looks on with open contempt for outsiders. Harpoon platforms overhang the cliffs on either side.

parts.body: Geirrvif has opened Valhalas to outsiders who have made a name for themselves. The vrykul who fell to them do not concern her: a warrior who can be bested is unworthy and fit only to be a lowly vargul. Valhalas, she says, is a place for combat of every kind against many kinds of foes, and she means to learn whether the newcomers are truly worthy.

parts.body: Word of one challenger's victories reached deep into Icecrown Citadel, and Prince Sandoval, a blood prince, came to Valhalas in person to end the matter. He fell in the pit. Gjonner, who held it an honor merely to kneel at the prince's feet, was sickened, and Geirrvif now greets the victor as a champion.

title: The Weeping Quarry
body: The Weeping Quarry, down the path southwest of the Shadow Vault, is a Scourge saronite quarry worked without rest by risen laborers, who pull immense amounts of ore from the ground. Ghoul lookouts watch over the pits, plaguehounds kept starving to sharpen their temper prowl the paths, and crystals scattered through the camp seem to serve as its defenses, not unlike the ziggurats of other Scourge holdings. Where all that saronite goes is a question the Ebon Blade means to answer.

title: Ymirheim
body: Ymirheim is the great frost vrykul city at the center of Icecrown, home of the Ymirjar, the vrykul the Lich King has deemed worthy to be his chosen. Val'kyr taskmistresses drive captives into the Saronite Mines beneath it, where an unknown voice whispers of fear and betrayal in the dark, blight falconers and proto-drakes hold the air, and automated spear guns inside the walls tear at anything that flies over. Alliance troops fight their way up the pass from the glacier to the east and the Kor'kron from the north, and both drop soldiers into the city from the air at heavy cost.

parts.body: The captives in the Saronite Mines are the Argent Crusade's own people, mining saronite for the Lich King day and night, and the Crusade's envoy aboard the gunship has promised Tirion Fordring to bring them out alive. Those freed so far come back half mad, complaining of voices in their heads.

title: The Broken Front and Mord'rethar
body: Mord'rethar, the Death Gate, is the first of the gates that bar the road to Icecrown Citadel. Flesh giants on its ramparts hurl boulders and ice at anything below, and plague cauldrons simmer in its western chamber. The field before it is the Broken Front, strewn with slain soldiers and their discarded helms and armor. Dying men still lie among the dead, Alliance and Horde alike, while geists, necromancers and abominations raise the fallen to fight again.

parts.body: The Broken Front was an Alliance assault on the gate, and it was broken when Horde soldiers fell upon it as well. Neither side has forgotten it, and the hatred born on this field now rides the gunships above Icecrown as surely as their war on the Scourge.

title: Aldur'thar and the Bombardment
body: Aldur'thar, the Desolation Gate, is the second gate on the road to the citadel, and the Cult of the Damned holds it. New initiates train at its southern end, an overseer runs each of its encampments, void summoners bind demonic minions in the north, and in the northwest cultists stir cauldrons of a brew that enslaves the will of every pledge who drinks it. Below the gate lies the Bombardment, where Scourge war machines, gargoyles and fleshrenders mass, and the Kor'kron hold the glacier's edge north of Ymirheim.

parts.body: The cultists of Aldur'thar stumbled upon something that could threaten every plan against the citadel. Their sect's leader, Alumeth, sacrificed himself in a ritual, and his followers channel power into his soul to make him a mighty adversary, Alumeth the Ascended. He has been struck down, but his spirit lingers.

Goblin engineers of the Horde found a new energy they call infra-green and used it to hide themselves close enough to bomb the Scourge, and the Alliance, which copied the trick, keeps a cloaked airport of its own nearby. Each side warns its pilots away from the other's dome.

title: The Valley of Lost Hope and Sindragosa's Fall
body: The Valley of Lost Hope stretches below the gunships between Ymirheim and Sindragosa's Fall, a valley of great strategic worth that crawls with decomposed ghouls, frostskull magi and bone giants, while scavenging geists pick apart the war machines left on the field. The Alliance holds a landing at its edge, and to the north lie the remains of an old army encampment. East beyond the valley, Sindragosa's Fall may be a graveyard of the blue dragonflight. There the Cult of the Damned, closely watched by undead vrykul necrolords, raises frost wyrms of the dreaded Frostbrood from the bones of blue dragons.

title: The Valley of Fallen Heroes and Corp'rethar
body: West of Aldur'thar the Valley of Fallen Heroes and the broad Icecrown Glacier lie open to the sky. Scourge converters wake the valley's dead, and banner-bearers fill the converted heroes with fearsome strength, while the gunships' recon fighters and scouts fly overhead. The Ironwall Rampart dominates the fields below, held by the necromancer Grimkor the Wicked and his cult disciples. South of it, on the ground called the Conflagration, the Lich King's elite form up before Corp'rethar, the Horror Gate and last barrier before the citadel: skeletal reavers that, it is feared, the Scourge can raise again whenever they fall, harbingers of horror on the battlements, and three crystal shards of horror, despair and suffering.

title: Blackwatch and the Fleshwerks
body: The Fleshwerks is the heart of the Scourge's production of ghouls, abominations and flesh giants. Skeletal constructors labor night and day in its abomination and flesh giant labs, blood orbs and vats of embalming fluid keep the parts fresh, and finished abominations stand chained to the pillars, waiting to march. Its prize is Morbidus, a flesh giant champion, and in the Sanctum of Reanimation the ghoul mastermind Doctor Sabnok keeps his creation Patches in chains. From Blackwatch, on a ridge above, Darkrider Arly of the Ebon Blade and Crusader Olakin Sainrith of the Argent Crusade plan its destruction.

parts.body: The jagged metal shards found in every ghoul of the Fleshwerks were cut from runed saronite plates forged by the skeletal runesmiths of Malykriss. The Scourge, Olakin judged, is desperate enough to make a weapon of anything, and these shards could pierce armor with enough force.

title: Malykriss: The Vile Hold

Skeletal runesmiths and saronite shapers work its forges and furnaces, lumbering atrocities and vargul brutes haul for them, iceskin sentries rest as stone along its walls, and lithe stalkers keep watch on the ramparts. In its yards a new generation of death knight initiates and adepts trains for the Lich King. Just to the west, on the Rise of Suffering within the Court of Bones, Vereth the Cunning of the Ebon Blade keeps a quiet watch on it all.

Northwest of the citadel the Cult of the Damned keeps the Cathedral of Darkness, guarded by chosen zealots and glacial bonelords and served by cult acolytes. In the shadow of the Lich King's walls, the dead outnumber everything else.

title: Icecrown Citadel
body: Icecrown Citadel, the Lich King's fortress, rises from the glacier crowned by the Frozen Throne. Citadel watchers guard its lower slopes, and below its walls an immense pit plunges several hundred feet into the ground, its purpose unknown but plainly of great importance to the Scourge. On the pit's lip waits a death knight, Orbaz Bloodbane, and Knights of the Ebon Blade keep watch close by. Beneath the citadel lie the Frozen Halls, the way into its depths.

parts.body: At the bottom of the pit lies Naz'anak, the Forgotten Depths, a cavern of dark water and ice where faceless ones lurk. A blast at the pit's lip sent the first visitor in a long while tumbling down into it, and beneath its water lies something pulsing, sealed in ice.

Aspirants train against dummies on the northern grounds and face their first challenge in the Aspirants' Ring, valiants meet Argent champions in the Argent Valiants' Ring on the western edge, and champions ride against one another in the Ring of Champions near the stables. Argent Confessor Paletress keeps a small chapel of the Light, the Knights of the Ebon Blade camp on the north side, and the Crusaders' Coliseum looms over the grounds.

title: The Lich King
body: The Lich King rules the Scourge from the Frozen Throne atop Icecrown Citadel. He was once Arthas Menethil, prince of Lordaeron, who took up the runeblade Frostmourne in Northrend, turned on his own people and at last joined with the Lich King Ner'zhul upon the throne. Those who fight him in Icecrown say he strikes recklessly, without care or caution, and one death knight sneers that the boy is not used to losing. His land is his fortress, and through his servants he watches much of what moves within it.

parts.body: When the Argent Crusade fought for Crusaders' Pinnacle, the Lich King's voice rang across the field, urging his creations to feast on the flesh of the living and calling on the crusaders to lay down their arms and surrender their souls. They did not, and the pinnacle was lost to him.

When Balargarde fell instead, he only told the victors that their efforts were for naught, for the frozen heart of Icecrown awaits.

Tirion struck at his heart with the Ashbringer all the same, and the Lich King fell to his knees, swearing that the old man would pay.

title: Highlord Darion Mograine
body: Highlord Darion Mograine is the master of the Knights of the Ebon Blade, the death knights who broke from the Lich King at Light's Hope Chapel when Tirion Fordring helped Mograine free them from his hold; Acherus, the Ebon Hold, is now the order's home. In Icecrown the order wages its own war of vengeance. Its knights hold Death's Rise and the Shadow Vault, keep watch on the Scourge from camps across the glacier and lend their counsel to the gunships, and Mograine himself moves among them.

parts.body: The Ebon Watcher who advised the Argent Crusade outside the Breach was Mograine himself. He served Tirion only to pay a debt, he told his knights, since the Highlord had freed them; once the Crusade had its foothold inside Icecrown, the Ebon Blade would part ways with it, for a different destiny awaits the order.

title: Grand Admiral Westwind
body: Barean Westwind, admiral of the Scarlet Fleet, is the master of the Scarlet Onslaught. By Lord-Commander Arete's account he presented himself unlooked for to High General Abbendis at New Hearthglen, undermined her and took the reins of command, and once she was dead he made a mysterious exit. Arete suspects he is somewhere on the Onslaught's island off Icecrown's coast, though none of the spies who came back could place him.

parts.body: A note in the grand admiral's own hand, taken from the Onslaught's baggage, settled it: he is on the island, keeping himself secluded for now. He writes of a glorious day soon to come, when the Scarlet Onslaught will wash over first the Lich King and then the rest of the world, and bring order to Azeroth at last.

title: Lady Nightswood
body: Lady Nightswood is a banshee. Once she had a home in the lush woods of Quel'Thalas, a husband and children, until the Lich King took it all away in the blink of an eye. She served him at the Shadow Vault until the Knights of the Ebon Blade broke his hold on her, and now she has gone into Jotunheim and taken possession of the vrykul's bone witch at Njorndar Village. She cannot strike at the Lich King directly, but from within the witch she means to pay him back threefold.

parts.body: Her first blow fell in the Underhalls, where Dr. Terrible worked on what he called the ultimate weapon, flesh giants like his prototype Nergeld. The doctor was drawn out and slain by his own creation. A fine poke in the eye for the Lich King, she said, but she meant to do better.

title: Crusader Bridenbrad
body: Crusader Bridenbrad is the hero of the Broken Front. When the Scourge came down upon the allied force there and its men scattered, he alone came back, dragging more than a dozen soldiers to safety one by one through the carnage. He has not come back since. He was last seen heading for the Silent Vigil in the far northeast of Icecrown, and Tirion Fordring wants him found so that he can be honored for his valor.

parts.body: He was found at the Silent Vigil beside his fire, carrying the plague of undeath. He warned his finder off, wanting no one else exposed, and confessed his only fear: not death, but serving the traitor Arthas after it. Tirion would not leave such a man to that fate and set out to find him salvation.

body: Crusader Olakin Sainrith is the Argent Crusade's contribution to the Ebon Blade's war on the Fleshwerks, sent to Blackwatch to stand beside Darkrider Arly. To him the dead are heroes who fell in defense of the living, and they must never be left to the Scourge's grisly work or raised against those who still live. He burns the corpses of the Scourge's victims with his own torch rather than leave them to it, and he studies every new horror the Fleshwerks turns out.

parts.body: The Scourge carried Olakin off, and Arly, to whom one crusader is much like another, sent for him only because the argents would not see it so. His body was recovered in pieces from the corpulent horrors of the Fleshwerks and stitched together on the slab in the Sanctum of Reanimation. He stands again, and Arly means him to remember that no one is rescued from the Scourge twice.

body: Matthias Lehner is a boy, or the ghost of one, who speaks out of the dark of Naz'anak, the Forgotten Depths, beneath Icecrown Citadel. He says he saw 'him' throw something all the way down there, saying he would not need it anymore and that it made him weak. Whoever touches it, the boy warns, will make 'him' angry, and 'he' will come looking for them unless they hide. Matthias is plainly afraid of him.

parts.body: At an old army encampment north of the Valley of Lost Hope he showed how the prince raised an army of the dead. Making armies out of corpses was easy, the boy said. The prince's true power was killing his own men, with whom he had shared many battles, because it had to be done.

title: Justicar Mariel Trueheart
body: Justicar Mariel Trueheart is the seneschal of the Argent Tournament, who welcomes every newcomer on behalf of the Argent Crusade. Many have been the divisions among those who oppose the Scourge, she reminds them, but the time has come for heroes of every banner to test their blades against one another before they face their mutual enemy. She sends Alliance newcomers to the Silver Covenant's Arcanist Taelis and those of the Horde to the Sunreavers' Magister Edien Sunhollow to be entered in the rolls.

parts.body: Those who rise through every challenge she formally enters in the champions' grand melee, where they may compete for the grand championship of the tournament. Every champion, she holds, must have a squire, and she appoints one of the Crusade's own to ride with each, proudly bearing the banner of every city that has named that hero its champion.

title: The Argent Crusade's March
body: The Argent Crusade has fought across continents, even worlds, to reach Icecrown, and here it faces its greatest challenge: the destruction of the Lich King and his Scourge. It fights divided from the Alliance and the Horde, who are at war with each other and lend it no support, and its envoys call on every volunteer to join the cause, for divided all will fall. Where both factions failed, the Crusade broke into Icecrown, but its breach was rebuffed at once and with force. The Lich King's answer was swift and brutal, and Highlord Tirion Fordring's Argent Vanguard now stands on the defensive.

parts.body: Bronze proto-drakes of Penumbrius's brood carried rescuers across the Breach to pull captured crusaders out of Scourgeholme. Arthas strikes recklessly, Tirion judged, without care or caution, and the Crusade had caught him off guard; it would bolster its defenses and weather the storm to come.

parts.body: The storm came out of the west, and the Vanguard held. Its blessed cannons broke the Scourge and its frost wyrms while Tirion fought on the field below. The valley was won back and the web walls torn down, and Tirion turned to the death knight called the Ebon Watcher, whose intimate knowledge of the Scourge would serve the push through the Breach.

The Argent Crusade stands inside the walls of Icecrown now, in open defiance of the Lich King, though Tirion knows that a long and arduous road to the gates of the citadel still lies ahead.

title: The War on Jotunheim
body: Duke Lankral, now master of the Shadow Vault, has turned the Ebon Blade against the vrykul of Jotunheim, over the mountains to the west. Every contest of ascension there sends its winner to Ymirheim and leaves its loser a vargul, and Lankral means to see far more vargul than Ymirjar come out of them. His knights humiliate Jotunheim's warriors on their own sparring ledge, burn its banners, plant Ebon Blade standards beside its dead, set its buildings ablaze from stolen proto-drakes and shoot its riders from the sky, day after day.

parts.body: Lankral's decree was read aloud in the hall of Thane Ufrang the Mighty, a patient strategist who liked to bide his time. Ufrang's answer was to attack the messenger, and he died for it. Against a foe that dwarfs his knights in stature and in numbers, Lankral says, the Ebon Blade must outthink the vrykul, and with Ufrang gone it has an advantage to press.

title: The Host of Suffering
body: At the Shadow Vault, Keritose Bloodblade has found that the Cult of the Damned, fleeing the Ebon Blade's slaughter, left eyes of dominion behind: tools that let any mind of some power command a lesser undead precisely. He has a use for them. The saronite quarry down the path to the southwest pulls immense amounts of ore from the ground, and Keritose wants to know what the Scourge is building with it. He begins by sending stolen undead in among its hounds, lookouts and crystals to weaken it from within before his gryphon riders strike.

parts.body: Papers seized in the chaos of the Ebon Blade's assault on the Weeping Quarry named the saronite's destination: Malykriss, the Vile Hold. Keritose read it as wounded pride. Arthas did not take the loss of his death knights well, he said, and the boy is not used to losing.

The Lich King is sparing nothing to replace Acherus and the knights he lost with it, and a citadel of pure saronite would be hard to destroy. The Ebon Blade means not to destroy it, but to halt the work and cut down the new order's leaders before they become a real threat.

title: The Skybreaker's Campaign
body: After its assault on the glacier from the ground came to grief, the Alliance carries its war in Icecrown aboard the Skybreaker, which it calls one of the most advanced works of engineering in Azeroth. From its decks High Captain Justin Bartlett lays the groundwork for the assault on Arthas, Chief Engineer Boltwrench keeps the ship in the air, and Absalan the Pious speaks for the Argent Crusade, whose help the Alliance knows it will need. The death knight Thassarian serves aboard as well, an advisor who knows the enemy from the inside.

parts.body: The Alliance's plans in Icecrown hinged on taking the first gate before the Horde could, and the secret attack on Mord'rethar ended as a rout on the Broken Front, with the Horde upon it. Bartlett has sworn the Horde will pay without mercy and readies his people for a war on two fronts.

title: Orgrim's Hammer's Campaign
body: Orgrim's Hammer, the Horde's gunship, flies out of the Scourge's reach high over the ground between Mord'rethar and Aldur'thar. The Alliance rushed into Icecrown unprepared, its officers say, while the Horde took its time and made ready. Sky-Reaver Korm Blackscar commands from the deck and swears vengeance on the Scourge and the Alliance alike, the goblin Chief Engineer Copperclaw crows over his inventions below, and Brother Keltan speaks for the Argent Crusade. title: The Heart of the Lich King
body: Below Icecrown Citadel lies a weakness in the Lich King's defenses, an opening in more ways than one, and the gunship's death knight adviser means to exploit it. The site is a pit that plunges deep into the ground beneath the citadel's walls, and hulking horrors stand guard over it. A small force has already been sent there with a stack of potent saronite bombs, made by the Scourge and taken from them, to secure the site and blow it open. Done right, a single blast could deal the Lich King's forces a heavy blow at the very foot of his fortress.

parts.body: The fuse burned far too fast. The blast hurt the Scourge badly, but it also threw one of the bombers down the pit into Naz'anak, the Forgotten Depths. There, beneath icy water, lay a pulsing organ sealed in ice that cut like a blade at a touch, and a boy's voice warned that its owner would come looking for whoever had touched it.

parts.body: The boy, Matthias Lehner, showed the rest in visions until there was no doubt: the frozen organ was the heart of Arthas, cast down the pit when he became king. Their death knight adviser had heard the tale before, but had never believed it more than a story. Now the news had to go in secret to Tirion Fordring, whose Crusade alone could be trusted free of the Cult.

Tirion struck the heart with the Ashbringer and was struck down in turn, and only the Ebon Blade's arrival brought his party out. He called it no failure: he had looked into the heart, and there is no Arthas Menethil anymore, only the Lich King.

title: The Argent Tournament
body: The Argent Crusade has called heroes of every banner to its tournament in northeastern Icecrown, so that the Alliance and the Horde may test their skill and valor against one another before they face the Scourge together. Each newcomer is entered in the rolls as an aspirant, by the Silver Covenant or by the Sunreavers, and learns to fight from the saddle with lance and shield against the training dummies on the northern grounds. Once proven, aspirants may ride on behalf of their capital cities, rising through the ranks of valiant and champion toward the grand melee.

parts.body: An aspirant who bests an Argent valiant in the Aspirants' Ring earns the rank of valiant and joins a capital city's delegation, training under its grand champion and sparring with other valiants for a place in the grand melee.

title: The Black Knight
body: A rider called the Black Knight has made a name for himself in the tournament's lists, and every combatant scheduled to face him has met an untimely end. His story of his own origins has proven a sham. Crusader Rhydalla of the Argent Crusade now means to prove that the deaths were murder and to tie them to him before he strikes again, and she knows a way to reveal how the dead truly died: a seer's crystal from the unbound seers of Crystalsong Forest, imbued with the power of the Light to cut through lies and deceit.

parts.body: The crystal told how three of them died: Lorien Sunblaze by poison, Sir Wendell Balfour burned alive, Conall Irongrip by a coward's strike. All three had sparred with the Black Knight and were to fight him. His squire Maloric, who went off each day as if to chop wood, carried the proof: poison, knives, torches and oil.
